title: PRO-V-R1: Reasoning Enhanced Programming Agent for RTL Verification
evidence_span: PRO-V-R1 couples LLM reasoning with programmatic verification tools, builds simulation-validated expert trajectories for supervised fine-tuning, and uses verification-specific reinforcement-learning rewards; the official description reports 57.7% functional correctness and 34.0% robust fault detection versus 25.7% and 21.8% for a base automatic-verification model.
problem: RTL verification consumes substantial development time, while proprietary-model workflows create cost and privacy barriers and open end-to-end autonomous verification remains limited.
method_or_artifact: Modular agentic RTL-verification system, simulation-validated trajectory construction, supervised fine-tuning, and tool-feedback reinforcement learning.
workload_or_benchmark: RTL functional verification and fault detection; designs, testbench suite, fault model, and evaluation budget are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: LLM plus simulation and programmatic verification tools; simulator, compute budget, and model size are unspecified.
metrics: Base-model comparison: 25.7% functional correctness and 21.8% robust fault detection
limits: The description omits RTL benchmark composition, simulator settings, fault taxonomy, model/training details, and statistical uncertainty.
Functional correctness and fault detection are distinct endpoints and may not generalize across design families.
Official description only; reproducibility, privacy, and tool-feedback claims require paper-level verification.

title: RISC-Q: A Generator for Real-Time Quantum Control System-on-Chips Compatible with RISC-V
evidence_span: RISC-Q is an open-source SpinalHDL generator for parameterized, modular quantum-control SoCs with a RISC-V-compatible programming interface; the description positions the generator for microsecond-latency feedback, nanosecond timing, and rapid hardware-software co-design, reporting better performance than existing QCSoCs with reduced development effort but no numeric values.
problem: Quantum-control systems need tight feedback and timing while platform diversity and fragmented toolchains make custom real-time hardware difficult to scale or adapt.
method_or_artifact: Parameterized SpinalHDL QCSoC generator with modular accelerators and a RISC-V-compatible software interface.
workload_or_benchmark: Real-time quantum control workloads; qubit count, control protocol, timing traces, and comparison platforms are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Quantum-control SoCs targeting microsecond feedback and nanosecond-precision GHz signals; FPGA/ASIC implementation, process, I/O, and control electronics are unspecified.
metrics: Performance improvement over existing QCSoCs claimed qualitatively
limits: No qubit scale, latency values, resource utilization, control fidelity, implementation target, or baseline identities are supplied.
Generator flexibility does not by itself establish timing closure or quantum-control fidelity.
Official description only; open-source artifact and hardware measurements require inspection.

title: COOL: A Cooling-Aware Point Transformer Framework for Thermal Prediction in Advanced 3D/3.5D IC Packaging
evidence_span: COOL represents dies, interposers, TIMs, and heat spreaders as annotated 3D point clouds containing geometry, material, and power, and adds a physics-informed boundary-condition loss for material and cooling interfaces; the official description reports 2.4% NMAE on a constructed multi-package benchmark and over 15.7x speedup versus commercial FEM solvers.
problem: 3D/3.5D packaging creates cross-layer heat coupling and complex cooling structures that make high-fidelity thermal solvers too slow for iterative co-design.
method_or_artifact: Cooling-aware point transformer, heterogeneous 3D point-cloud representation, explicit geometric boundaries, and physics-informed boundary-condition loss.
workload_or_benchmark: Constructed benchmark of multi-package thermal designs; package geometries, power distributions, materials, and held-out split are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Advanced 3D/3.5D packages with dies, interposers, TIMs, heat spreaders, and cooling structures; thermal properties and solver settings are unspecified.
metrics: More than 15.7x speedup versus commercial FEM solvers
limits: The description omits benchmark size, spatial resolution, material parameters, boundary conditions, FEM hardware, and error distribution.
Speedup and NMAE trade off fidelity, preprocessing, and solver convergence; transfer to unseen package/cooling structures is unknown.
Official description only; thermal validity requires full-paper and independent review.

title: S2CIM: A Secure-Computation and Secure-Storage Compute-in-Memory Architecture with Circuit-Algorithm Co-Design for Efficient and Trustworthy Edge Inference
evidence_span: S²CIM uses FeFET nonvolatile CIM with Affine-Transform Splitting to protect stored weights and online inputs without exposing plaintext keys, and a Drain-Input Gate-Scan 1FeFET-1R circuit for signed multi-bit MAC; the official description reports a 16× area-efficiency improvement, 6.7× lower energy per MAC, 97.4% encrypted ViT accuracy, and 50% attack success under stated threat models.
problem: Nonvolatile CIM exposes stored weights and plaintext inputs in untrusted edge environments, while prior in-memory encryption can require plaintext keys and incur large area overhead.
method_or_artifact: FeFET-based secure CIM, Affine-Transform Splitting for offline/online obfuscation, and Drain-Input Gate-Scan signed multi-bit MAC circuitry.
workload_or_benchmark: 16×16 CIM macro and encrypted Vision Transformer inference; model, dataset, attack procedures, and accuracy/security baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: FeFET 1FeFET-1R nonvolatile CIM macro; process, endurance, peripheral circuits, ADC/DAC, and attack access are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 6.7x lower energy per MAC
50% attack success rate under all stated threat models
limits: The description omits process node, area definition, peripheral overhead, threat-model details, key management, dataset/model, and accuracy degradation.
A 50% attack success rate is not interpretable without attack baseline and random-guess reference.
Official description only; circuit security and measured energy require paper-level verification.

title: TierANNS: Scalable Graph-Based ANNS with CXL-Enabled Tiered Data Placement
evidence_span: TierANNS/COGA uses a CXL-tailored priority queue to improve bandwidth utilization and bridge CXL latency, plus queue-hint-driven tiered index placement for speculative access; the official description presents scalable high-speed graph ANNS but supplies no numeric throughput, latency, recall, or capacity results.
problem: Graph-based approximate nearest-neighbor search requires random access and large memory capacity, making single-tier memory deployments difficult to scale.
method_or_artifact: CXL-aware priority queue, tiered graph-index data layout, and queue-hint-guided speculative access placement.
workload_or_benchmark: Large-scale graph-based approximate nearest-neighbor search; dataset, graph construction, recall target, query rate, and memory capacity are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: CXL-extended memory with host/fast tiers and a graph-search pipeline; CXL generation, link bandwidth, device latency, and CPU platform are unspecified.
baselines: conventional graph-based ANNS on single-tier memory
metrics: Scalable/high-speed ANNS claimed qualitatively; numeric throughput, latency, recall, and capacity are not supplied
limits: No numeric performance, recall, memory-capacity, CXL bandwidth, or queue-overhead conditions are supplied.
Speculative placement may trade memory footprint and recall/latency under changing query distributions.
Official description only; system comparison requires paper-level verification.
